mainTopic: Guarantors for loans and כתובות, and how creditors collect from orphans (זיבורית, עידית, and adult heirs)
overview: The amud opens by sorting guarantors. Everyone agrees a קבלן for a loan is obligated, while a ערב for a loan and a קבלן for a כתובה are disputed. The הלכה is that every guarantor is obligated even if the main party has no property. The one exception is a ערב for a כתובה, who is never obligated, because he only did a מצוה and the woman lost nothing. רבינא then refutes מר זוטרא, showing that a כתובה is paid from זיבורית even when collected from the husband himself. Next comes רב נחמן's ruling that a lender collecting from יתומים gets only זיבורית, even if his document promises better land. אביי supports it, but רבא argues that orphans only stay at the Torah-level rule, so a best-land clause should be honored even against them. רבא's view survives challenges from two ברייתות, one about injured parties and one about 'even if it is עידית'. Finally רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks whether the orphans' rule covers adult heirs too. A proof from אביי קשישא is pushed aside, and the ruling begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Which guarantor cases are agreed and which are disputed
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a קבלן for a loan is obligated. A ערב for a loan and a קבלן for a כתובה are in dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: An unconditional guarantor for a loan is obligated according to everyone. A regular guarantor for a loan, and an unconditional guarantor for a כתובה, are subject to a disagreement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sorts guarantor cases into groups: one case that everyone agrees on, and two cases that are argued about. It is setting up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קבלן is the strongest kind of guarantor, so for a regular loan nobody argues that he is obligated. The argument only starts with the weaker ערב on a loan, and with a קבלן on a כתובה, where no money was actually handed over.

keyTerms.meaning: An unconditional guarantor whom the creditor may go to directly
A regular guarantor who backs up the main debtor
A creditor; here it means a loan situation
Becomes obligated or bound to pay
The marriage contract money owed to the wife
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: There are four cases in play: a ערב or a קבלן, each for a loan or for a כתובה. Here one is agreed (קבלן for a loan) and two are disputed. The fourth, a ערב for a כתובה, was settled earlier and comes back in the הלכה.

phrases.english: An unconditional guarantor for a creditor:
according to everyone, he becomes obligated.
A regular guarantor for a creditor,
and an unconditional guarantor for a כתובה: they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלָן דְּבַעַל חוֹב דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of guarantors for loans and כתובות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קבלן for a loan is obligated according to all; a ערב for a loan and a קבלן for a כתובה are disputed.

steps.title: The two opinions in the dispute
steps.stepSummary: One view says the guarantor is obligated even if the main party has no property. The other says he is obligated only if the main party has property.
steps.simpleTranslation: One opinion holds that even if the borrower has no property, the guarantor is obligated. Another opinion holds that if the borrower has property the guarantor is obligated, and if not, he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two sides of the disagreement over the disputed cases from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole dispute depends on one detail: does the main party own property? The first view ignores this detail, and the guarantor is always bound. The second view makes the guarantor's obligation depend on it.

keyTerms.meaning: There is one who says (an unnamed opinion)
The borrower
Property, possessions
He has / he does not have

phrases.english: There is one who says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ נִכְסֵי לְלֹוֶה –
phrases.english: even though the borrower has no property,
the guarantor becomes obligated.
And there is one who says:
if he has property, the guarantor becomes obligated;
phrases.notes: "He" here is the main party, meaning the borrower or the husband.

phrases.english: if he does not have property, the guarantor does not become obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the content of the dispute mentioned in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: View 1: the guarantor is obligated even without the main party's property. View 2: he is obligated only if the main party has property.

steps.title: The final ruling on guarantors
steps.stepSummary: In all these cases the guarantor is obligated even if the main party has no property, except a ערב for a כתובה, who is never obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: in all of them, even if he has no property, the guarantor is obligated. The exception is a guarantor for a כתובה, who is not obligated even if the husband does have property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical הלכה, siding with the first view and naming one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows the stricter view from step 2: whether the main party owns property does not matter. The ערב for a כתובה is the opposite extreme. He is free even when the husband has property, so his exemption has nothing to do with property at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה, the final ruling
In all of them
Except for

steps.whatToRemember: Every guarantor is obligated, even if the main party has no property, except a ערב for a כתובה, who is never obligated.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: in all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ – מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד;
phrases.english: even though he has no property, the guarantor becomes obligated,
except for a regular guarantor for a כתובה,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית לֵיהּ – לָא מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד.
phrases.english: who, even if the husband has property, does not become obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute of step 2 and adds the exception.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All guarantors are obligated regardless of the main party's property, except a ערב for a כתובה, who is never obligated.

steps.title: Why is the guarantor for a כתובה exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ערב for a כתובה is treated differently. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption in step 3 looks strange, since he is free even when the husband has property. So the גמרא needs a reason that has nothing to do with property.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A regular guarantor for a כתובה

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the exception in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a ערב for a כתובה is not obligated even if the husband has property.

steps.title: He only did a מצוה and she lost nothing
steps.stepSummary: The ערב for a כתובה was doing a מצוה, and the woman gave up nothing because of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was doing a מצוה, and he did not cause her to lose anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two reasons for the exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, he stepped in to help the marriage happen, which is a מצוה, and not to seriously take on a debt. Second, in a loan the lender hands over money because of the guarantor. Here the woman hands over nothing, so there is no loss for him to cover.

keyTerms.meaning: A good deed, here helping a marriage come about
Anything
Caused her a loss

steps.whatToRemember: A ערב for a כתובה is exempt because he did a מצוה and the woman lost nothing because of him.

phrases.english: It is a מצוה that he did,
phrases.notes: He helped the marriage happen, so he is not seen as really taking on a debt.

phrases.english: and he did not cause her to lose anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He acted only to do a מצוה, and the woman lost nothing in reliance on him.

steps.title: רבינא brings the original reason for the זיבורית rule
steps.stepSummary: רבינא recalls why the חכמים said a כתובה is paid from the poorest land: a woman wants to marry more than a man does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear from the original reason for our תקנה: more than a man wants to marry, a woman wants to be married.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא returns to the earlier question of when a כתובה is paid from זיבורית. He sets up a proof from the reason the חכמים gave for that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a כתובה is collected from the worst land. מר זוטרא limited this to collecting from יתומים. רבינא points to the stated reason for the rule, which says nothing about יתומים.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning, the root
A rule set up by the חכמים
To be married (said of the woman)

phrases.english: רבינא said:
Come and hear from the root of our תקנה:
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a כתובה is paid from the poorest land, and the reason given for it earlier.

phrases.english: more than a man wants to marry,
a woman wants to be married.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא תָּא שְׁמַע מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּתַקַּנְתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the guarantor discussion and returns to the earlier זיבורית topic.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the זיבורית rule for a כתובה applies even when she collects from the husband himself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The original reason for the תקנה: a woman wants to marry more than a man does.

steps.title: If it were about orphans, the reason would mention orphans
steps.stepSummary: If the rule applied only to collecting from יתומים, the reason should have been that they are יתומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think the rule is only when collecting from orphans, then the reason should be because they are orphans!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא finishes his proof by turning it against מר זוטרא's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the חכמים gave is about the woman's own wish to marry, and that applies with the husband too. A rule limited to יתומים would have been explained by the special protection given to יתומים, and no such reason was given. So the rule must apply even when she collects from the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind, you might think
Orphans, the husband's heirs
Because of

phrases.english: And if you think the rule is only when collecting from orphans,
then this would be because they are orphans!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the reason quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's view that the זיבורית rule applies only when collecting from יתומים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stated reason has nothing to do with יתומים. A rule only for יתומים would have been explained by their being יתומים.

steps.title: מר זוטרא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares מר זוטרא's view firmly refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of מר זוטרא is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the matter: רבינא's proof defeats מר זוטרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated word תיובתא marks a final, decisive refutation. The result is that a כתובה is paid from זיבורית even when the woman collects from the husband himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; said twice, it means a conclusive one
The lowest-quality land, from which a כתובה is paid

steps.whatToRemember: The זיבורית rule for a כתובה is not limited to יתומים. It applies even when collecting from the husband, and מר זוטרא is refuted.

phrases.english: The refutation of מר זוטרא is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבינא's proof as decisive.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כתובה is collected from זיבורית even from the husband himself; מר זוטרא's limit to יתומים is rejected.

steps.title: Collecting from orphans only from the poorest land, even with a best-land clause
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, quoting רב נחמן, rules that a lender collecting from יתומים gets only זיבורית, even if the loan document says he may collect from better land (שבח).
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן said in the name of רב נחמן: when a loan document is brought to collect from orphans, the lender collects only from the poorest land, even if the document gives him a right to better land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from מר זוטרא in the name of רב נחמן. The topic is how a lender collects a loan from orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a special clause (שבח) in the document lets the lender take better land. Here רב נחמן says that when collecting from יתומים, the clause does not help, and the lender is limited to the poorest land. This is the ruling the rest of this section will test.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document
Orphans; here, the heirs of a borrower who died
A clause in the document that improves the lender's rights, letting him collect from better land
The poorest-quality land

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman said
in the name of Rav Nachman:
A loan document that is brought against orphans

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שֶׁבַח,
phrases.english: even though a clause for better land is written in it,
he collects only from the poorest land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier view of מר זוטרא was refuted, the גמרא brings another ruling in his name on a related topic: collecting from orphans.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender collecting from יתומים collects only from זיבורית, even if the document has a שבח clause.

steps.title: אביי supports the ruling from the normal rule for lenders
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that a lender normally collects from בינונית but from orphans only from זיבורית. If orphans don't even have to give middle land, they certainly don't have to give the best land, even with a better-land clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: you can see this is true. A lender's rule is to collect from middle land, but from orphans he collects from the poorest land.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings support for רב נחמן's ruling. He points to the general rule that orphans lower what a lender may collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every lender usually gets middle land, yet from orphans he drops to the poorest land. אביי reasons that the orphans' protection always pushes the lender down. So even a lender promised better land should drop to the poorest land when collecting from orphans.

keyTerms.meaning: Know: an opening word that introduces a supporting proof
A lender (creditor)
Middle-quality land

phrases.english: Abaye said: know that this is so,
for a lender's rule is to collect from middle land,
but from orphans, from the poorest land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that a שבח clause does not help against orphans.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The general rule: a lender collects from בינונית, but from orphans only from זיבורית.

steps.title: רבא rejects the comparison: by Torah law a lender gets the poorest land
steps.stepSummary: רבא says אביי's comparison does not work. By Torah law every lender collects from זיבורית, so orphans do not lower him at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: how can you compare these? By Torah law, a lender collects from the poorest land!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's proof. He says the basic rule for any lender, by Torah law, is the poorest land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed orphans lower the lender from middle land to poor land. רבא says the true starting point is the poorest land, by Torah law. So orphans are not lowering anything; they just keep the original Torah rule. That removes the basis of אביי's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you say that? A strong rejection of a comparison
By Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think orphans get a special lowering. רבא's point is that orphans just stay at the basic Torah rule, while everyone else got an increase from the רבנן.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: how can you compare these?!
A lender's rule by Torah law is the poorest land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's comparison between an ordinary lender and a lender with a שבח clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי treated בינונית as the basic rule. In truth the Torah-level rule is זיבורית, so orphans do not lower the lender at all.

steps.title: עולא's source: the poorest land by Torah law, middle land by the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רבא backs his claim with עולא: the פסוק shows a lender gets the least valuable item, so the poorest land. The רבנן raised this to בינונית so people would keep lending, but left orphans at the Torah rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows עולא, who said: by Torah law a lender collects from the poorest land, as it says, 'You shall stand outside, and the man…' What does a person usually bring out? The least valuable of his things. Why did the חכמים say a lender collects from middle land? So people will not stop lending. But for orphans, the רבנן left it at the Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his point from עולא's teaching. It explains where the poorest-land rule comes from and why lenders usually get more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the borrower bringing out a pledge, and a person brings out his cheapest item, so the Torah gives the lender the poorest land. The רבנן raised lenders to middle land so lending would not dry up. They did not make this increase for orphans, so orphans stay at the Torah-level rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The least valuable of one's things
Locking the door before borrowers: making people stop giving loans
They left it at the Torah law

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea: the orphans' rule is not a special reduction. It only means the רבנן's increase does not apply to them, and that is the basis for רבא's final challenge.

phrases.english: As Ulla taught, for Ulla said:
By Torah law, a lender collects from the poorest land,
as it says: 'You shall stand outside, and the man, etc.'
What does a person usually bring out?
The least valuable of his things.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה טַעַם אָמְרוּ בַּעַל חוֹב בְּבֵינוֹנִית?
phrases.english: And why did they say a lender collects from middle land?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּנְעוֹל דֶּלֶת בִּפְנֵי לֹוִין –
phrases.english: So as not to lock the door in front of borrowers.
And regarding orphans, the Rabbis left it at the Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבא's claim in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that by Torah law a lender collects from זיבורית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's reading of דברים 24:11: a borrower brings out the least valuable item.

steps.title: With a best-land clause, even orphans should pay from the best land
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that when the document promises עידית, the lender's Torah-level right is the best land, so he should collect עידית even from orphans. This challenges רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, since by Torah law his right is to the best land, then even from orphans he should collect from the best land!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא turns his argument against the ruling itself. He says a lender with a best-land clause should get the best land even from orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Orphans only keep the Torah-level rule, not a lower one. When the borrower himself promised the best land, that promise is the Torah-level right. So the orphans' protection, which only blocks the רבנן's increase, gives no reason to lower him. This directly challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The best-quality land
But here: turning from the general rule to the case at hand

steps.whatToRemember: Orphans don't lower a lender below the Torah rule; they just don't get the רבנן's increase. So if the lender's own document gives him the best land by Torah law, רבא says he gets it even from orphans.

phrases.english: But here,
phrases.notes: Here means the case of a document with a best-land clause.

phrases.english: since his right by Torah law is to the best land,
even from orphans, too, he should collect from the best land!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּדִינֵיהּ מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בְּעִידִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses עולא's framework from step 12 to challenge the ruling of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling (step 9) that a שבח clause does not help against orphans.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Orphans only stay at the Torah-level rule. With a שבח clause, the Torah-level right is עידית, so the lender should collect עידית even from orphans.

steps.title: A teaching about injured parties challenges רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא taught by אברם חוזאה says that even injured parties (ניזקין) collect only זיבורית from orphans. Injured parties collect עידית by Torah law, so it looks like the רבנן did push orphans below the Torah level, against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, didn't אברם חוזאה teach: We collect from orphans' property only from the poorest land, even when the collectors are injured parties? But injured parties, by Torah law, collect from the best land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא. It shows orphans paying less than the Torah-level right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the רבנן left orphans at the Torah-level right and did not lower them further. But injured parties have a Torah right to עידית, and the ברייתא says they still get only זיבורית from orphans. So the רבנן did lower orphans below the Torah level, which would also support רב נחמן's ruling for a lender with an עידית clause.

keyTerms.meaning: Collect payment (of a debt)
The property of orphans (inherited from the father who owed)
Injured parties: people whose property was damaged
By Torah law
But didn't [so-and-so] teach (introduces a ברייתא as a challenge)

phrases.english: And according to Rava, didn't Avram Ḥoza'a teach:
We do not collect from the property of orphans
except from the poorest land,
and even if they are injured parties.
phrases.notes: He means even when the people collecting are victims of damage that the orphans' father caused.

phrases.english: But injured parties —
their law, by Torah law, is to collect from the best land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle רבא built in steps 11–13, that orphans are never lowered below the Torah-level right.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the רבנן left orphans at the Torah level and did not lower them.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Injured parties are entitled to עידית by Torah law, yet the ברייתא gives them only זיבורית from orphans. So orphans were lowered below the Torah level.

steps.title: The teaching is about a special case of land values
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא speaks about a case where the injured party's best land is equal in quality to the damager's poorest land.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what case are we dealing here? Where the injured party's best land was equal to the damager's poorest land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins defending רבא by narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case. The next line will explain why this case matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land quality can be measured against the injured party's fields or against the damager's fields. Here the orphans' poorest land is as good as the injured party's best land, so 'זיבורית' and 'עידית' can describe the same field depending on whose land you compare to.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (narrows a source to a specific case)
The injured party
The one who caused the damage

steps.confusionAlert: The 'מזיק' here is really the orphans. Their father caused the damage, and they now pay from what they inherited.

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing here?
For example, where the best land of the injured party
was like the poorest land of the one who caused the damage;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by limiting the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to give injured parties less than their Torah-level right of עידית.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this case the orphans' זיבורית is just as good as the injured party's עידית, so the injured party is not really getting less than the Torah level.

steps.title: Following רבי ישמעאל, orphans stay at the Torah level
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל: by Torah law land quality is measured against the injured party's land. The רבנן improved this to the damager's land, but for orphans they kept the Torah rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows רבי ישמעאל, who says: By Torah law we assess by the injured party's land. For the betterment of the world, the רבנן enacted that we assess by the damager's land. But for orphans, the רבנן left it at Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows the ברייתא matches רבא's principle that orphans are kept exactly at Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, the Torah only requires land that counts as 'best' compared to the injured party's fields. So the orphans' זיבורית, which equals that, fully satisfies the Torah. The רבנן's upgrade to the damager's own עידית does not apply to orphans, so they stay at the Torah level, not below it, and רבא's principle stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We assess / evaluate (whose land sets the standard)
The betterment of the world; a rabbinic enactment for the good of society
The רבנן enacted
They left it at the Torah-law level

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישמעאל, orphans pay damages from land that is 'best' compared to the injured party's fields. That is exactly the Torah level, so the ברייתא fits רבא's rule: the רבנן did not upgrade orphans, but they also did not lower them below the Torah.

phrases.english: And this follows Rabbi Yishmael, who says:
By Torah law we assess by the injured party's land,
and for the betterment of the world
the Rabbis enacted that we assess by the damager's land —
but regarding orphans
the Rabbis left it at Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 15 by naming the תנא whose view makes the case work.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Injured parties were thought to have a Torah right to the damager's own עידית, so getting זיבורית from orphans seemed to lower them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי ישמעאל, the Torah right is measured by the injured party's land. Orphans stay at that level, which matches רבא's principle, just like a lender in עולא's teaching (step 12).
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer keeps רבא's whole approach alive. The orphans' rule means 'no rabbinic upgrade', not 'go below the Torah'.

steps.title: Another teaching seems to say orphans pay זיבורית even when עידית is written
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר ניותאה says orphans pay only from זיבורית 'even if it is עידית'. The גמרא suggests this means even when the document promises עידית, which directly contradicts רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But didn't רבי אליעזר ניותאה teach: We collect from orphans' property only from the poorest land, even if it is best land. What does 'even if it is best land' mean? Doesn't it mean even though best land is written in the document?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to רבא from a second ברייתא. Its wording seems to match רב נחמן's ruling exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'even if it is עידית' is unclear, so the גמרא asks what it means. The natural reading is a loan document that promises עידית. If so, the ברייתא says orphans still pay only זיבורית, which is רב נחמן's ruling and the opposite of רבא's conclusion in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so?! (opens a challenge)
Is it not…? (introduces the suggested reading)
Even though
The (loan) document

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rabbi Eliezer Nayota'a teach:
We do not collect from the property of orphans
except from the poorest land,
and even if it is best land.
What does "even if it is best land" mean?
Doesn't it mean even though
best land is written in the document?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא survived the first challenge (steps 14–16), a second ברייתא challenges him directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's conclusion (step 13) that a lender with an עידית clause collects עידית even from orphans.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read 'even if it is עידית' as 'even if עידית is written in the document'. Then the ברייתא says orphans pay only זיבורית despite the clause, which is רב נחמן's ruling and the opposite of רבא's.

steps.title: The word 'עידית' in the ברייתא means low-value strips of good land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reading that the ברייתא is talking about a document that promises עידית. 'עידית' there means שפאי עידית, as in רבא's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'עידית' mean here? Strips of good land, like רבא taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the attack against רבא. The ברייתא's phrase 'even if it is עידית' was never about a document that promised good land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, 'even if it is עידית' was read as 'even if the document promised עידית.' Now the גמרא says it describes the land itself: strips of good soil that are awkward to farm or guard, so they are worth less. The orphans may pay with this kind of land, and that says nothing against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Narrow strips of good soil that are hard to farm or guard, so they are worth less on the market
No. It opens a rejection of the suggestion that came before
Like רבא's teaching. The גמרא is about to quote it as support

steps.confusionAlert: 'עידית' here does not mean truly valuable land. The soil is good, but the plots are so awkward that they are worth even less than plain זיבורית.

phrases.english: No; what is meant by 'superior-quality land'?
Strips of superior-quality land, as in the teaching of רבא.
phrases.notes: Good soil, but cut into strips that are hard to work or guard, so they are worth little.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers by rejecting the reading of רבי אליעזר ניותאה's ברייתא that was used against רבא in step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the suggested meaning of 'even if it is עידית'. The ברייתא's ruling itself stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed 'עידית' meant a document promising good land. It actually means low-value strips of good soil.

steps.title: רבא's teaching on damaged land and strips of good land
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches two rules. If someone damaged זיבורית, he pays from עידית. If he damaged שפאי עידית, he pays from בינונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if he damaged poor land, the victim collects from the best land. If he damaged strips of good land, the victim collects from middle land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבא's teaching to show that שפאי עידית is a real category with its own value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who damages even זיבורית pays from עידית, as a penalty. But strips of good land are worth even less than זיבורית, so damaging them is treated more lightly: he pays only from בינונית. This shows that שפאי עידית ranks below ordinary poor land in value.

keyTerms.meaning: He caused damage
He collects (payment)
Middle-quality land

phrases.english: As רבא said:
If one damaged inferior-quality land, the victim collects from superior-quality land.
If he damaged strips of superior-quality land, the victim collects from intermediate-quality land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the category שפאי עידית named in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damaging זיבורית means paying from עידית. Damaging שפאי עידית means paying only from בינונית, because those strips are worth less than זיבורית.

steps.title: For orphans, the רבנן kept the Torah-level rule
steps.stepSummary: With orphans, the רבנן left the law at the Torah level. So orphans may pay with the lowest-value land, even strips of good soil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with orphans, the רבנן left it at the Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. For orphans, the רבנן did not apply their usual improvement for the creditor, so the orphans may pay with the lowest-value land, including strips of good soil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, an ordinary creditor collects from זיבורית. The רבנן raised the creditor to בינונית, but for orphans they kept the Torah rule. So the ברייתא only allows the orphans to pay with the cheapest land, and it never pushes anyone below the Torah level. רבא's position stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In the case of orphans
They left it at the Torah-level law

steps.whatToRemember: 'Even if it is עידית' means strips of good soil that are worth little. The orphans' rule keeps the creditor at the Torah level, so רבא's ruling stands.

phrases.english: And with regard to orphans,
the רבנן left it at the Torah law.
phrases.notes: By Torah law a creditor collects from the poorest land, so the orphans may pay at that level.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's category to orphans and answers the challenge from step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the ברייתא is about the value of the land, not the wording of the document
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets orphans pay זיבורית even when the document promised עידית, which would go against רבא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only lets orphans pay with the cheapest land, such as strips of good soil, which is still the Torah level
steps.kashyaTarget: The challenge from רבי אליעזר ניותאה's ברייתא against רבא

steps.title: Does the orphans' rule mean only minors, or adults too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that orphans pay only from זיבורית. רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks whether 'orphans' means only minors or also adult heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We collect from orphans' property only from poor land.' רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked: the 'orphans' they spoke of, are they minors, or even adults?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words and opens a new question about who counts as 'orphans' for this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule protects orphans when a creditor comes to collect their father's debt. The question is whether this protection is only for young heirs, or for any heir after the borrower dies. The next two steps give the reasoning for each side.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not collect payment
The property of orphans (the heirs)
He asked, raising an open question
Minors / adults

phrases.english: One does not collect from the property of orphans
phrases.notes: These are the words of our משנה.

phrases.english: except from inferior-quality land.
רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked:
The 'orphans' that they spoke of, are they minors,
or even adults?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עידית discussion and goes back to the משנה's wording
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the word 'orphans' in the משנה covers only minors or adult heirs as well

steps.title: First side: a special enactment just for young orphans
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the rule is a kindness the רבנן made for orphans. If so, it would be only for minors, who need protection, and not for adults.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it an enactment the רבנן made for orphans? Then the רבנן made it for minors, not for adults.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first side of the question: the rule might be a special protection for helpless young heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is to protect orphans, then only minors need it, since they cannot look after themselves. Adult heirs can handle their own affairs, so the רבנן would not have made it for them.

keyTerms.meaning: An enactment made by the רבנן
The רבנן made (it)

phrases.aramaic: תַּקַּנְתָּא הִיא דַּעֲבוּד רַבָּנַן גַּבֵּי יַתְמֵי –
phrases.english: Is it an enactment that the רבנן made for orphans?
Then the רבנן made it for minors,
and the רבנן did not make it for adults.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּקַּנְתָּא הִיא דַּעֲבוּד רַבָּנַן גַּבֵּי יַתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first possible reason behind the question in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule is a protective enactment for orphans, which would limit it to minors

steps.title: Second side: the lender never thinks about the borrower dying
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe the reason is different. The improvement to בינונית was made so lenders would not stop lending. A lender never plans for the borrower dying, so that worry does not matter after death, and the rule would apply to adult heirs too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is because the lender does not think that the borrower will die and his property will pass to the orphans. Only if he did would it lock the door. So it applies even to adults too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side. Here the rule is not a favor to orphans. It comes from how the lender's improvement works in the first place, so it would cover adult heirs as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן raised creditors to בינונית so that lenders would not 'lock the door' on borrowers. But no lender thinks the borrower will die and his land go to heirs, so that worry does not cover heirs. With no reason to improve things, the creditor stays at Torah-level זיבורית against any heir, adult or minor.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. It introduces the other side of a question
It does not enter his mind
Locking the door: lenders stop lending to borrowers
Therefore

steps.whyThisMatters: The two sides show two different reasons for the orphans' rule. One is protecting the weak. The other is that the reason behind the creditor's improvement does not reach heirs. Each reason gives a different answer about adult heirs.

phrases.english: Or perhaps
it is because it does not enter the lender's mind

phrases.aramaic: דְּמִית לֹוֶה וְנָפְלִי נִכְסֵי קַמֵּי יַתְמֵי;
phrases.english: that the borrower will die and his property will pass to the orphans;
that it would amount to locking the door.
phrases.notes: He means: only if the lender worried about this would it stop him from lending. Since he doesn't, there is no need to give him more.

phrases.english: Therefore it applies even to adults too?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מַסֵּיק אַדַּעְתָּא דְּמַלְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other possible reason, which would lead to the opposite answer from step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule exists because the 'locking the door' worry does not apply to heirs, which would include adult heirs

steps.title: A teaching says 'orphans' includes adults
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from אביי קשישא: when the רבנן say 'orphans,' they mean adults, and certainly minors.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what אביי the Elder taught: the 'orphans' the רבנן spoke about are adults, and of course minors too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 21 by quoting a teaching that 'orphans' includes adult heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'orphans' in the language of the רבנן always includes adults, then the משנה's rule that orphans pay from זיבורית would apply to adult heirs too. That would match the second side of the question (step 23), that the rule exists because lenders do not plan for the borrower's death.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי the Elder, an earlier sage, different from the famous אביי
Orphans; here, the heirs of someone who died
Adults
Minors

phrases.english: Come and hear:
what אביי the Elder taught:
The orphans that they spoke of
phrases.notes: 'They' means the רבנן, the sages who made rules about orphans.

phrases.english: are adults,
and needless to say, minors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source to settle the question posed in steps 21-23.
steps.raayaObject: That the זיבורית rule for orphans applies to adult heirs as well.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of אביי קשישא saying that 'orphans' in the words of the רבנן means adults, and certainly minors.

steps.title: Maybe that teaching is only about the oath
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. אביי קשישא's teaching may refer only to the oath taken when collecting from heirs, where an adult is like a minor, and not to the זיבורית rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe that teaching is only about an oath, because an adult is like a minor when it comes to his father's business. About paying from זיבורית, though, it may not apply to adults.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The teaching could be talking about a different law, so it does not answer our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an oath, an adult heir is no better off than a minor, because neither knows the details of his father's dealings, so it makes sense to treat both the same. The זיבורית rule might be a special kindness for minors only, as in step 22. So the teaching does not prove that adults also pay from זיבורית.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; introduces a pushback on a proof
These words; this rule applies only to a certain case
Oath
The lowest-quality land

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that adults are never 'orphans.' It is only saying that the teaching might be about the oath, so it cannot settle the זיבורית question.

phrases.english: But perhaps these words apply
to the matter of an oath,
phrases.notes: A lender who collects from heirs has to swear he was never paid. That is the oath meant here.

phrases.english: because an adult, in his father's matters,
is like a minor.
But regarding זיבורית, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of אביי קשישא's teaching as proof for the זיבורית question. The teaching itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teaching may be limited to the oath, where adults and minors are equally unaware of their father's dealings. It does not have to extend to the זיבורית rule, which may be a kindness for minors only.

steps.title: Opening the final ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to state the practical הלכה on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to give the final ruling, which comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof failed, so the question was not settled from a source. The גמרא now moves straight to the practical decision instead of looking for more proofs.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is; introduces the final practical ruling

phrases.english: And the הלכה is:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof is rejected, the גמרא turns to the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling itself comes at the start of the next amud. This line only opens it.
